title: Encryption Safeguards: Operational Runbook for KMS/HSM, BYOK and Rotation
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures operational steps, scripts, and validation checks for key custody (hosted KMS, HSM-backed BYOK), rotation ceremonies for KEKs/DEKs, audit logging schema, and SIEM export mappings. Intended audience: SREs, infra engineers, security on-call, and compliance auditors.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers encryption-at-rest for customer data and telemetry stored in S3-compatible blob stores and databases.
- Assumes RBAC v2 policies are already in place for service identities (service accounts) and human roles. See RBAC v2 checklist section.
- Does not replace vendor-specific HSM operator manuals (YubiHSM/Thales/AWS CloudHSM), but includes operational commands that we use in the field.
- Focused on symmetric key rotation (KEK = key-encryption-key, DEK = data-encryption-key). Asymmetric (signing) key rotation is out of scope for this doc.

Quick architecture summary (informal):
- DEKs are generated per-object or per-bucket and stored encrypted in metadata. DEKs are encrypted with a KEK that lives in a KMS or HSM.
- KEKs: in Hosted KMS mode we use Redwood-managed keys; in Dedicated/Private we support customer BYOK wrapped by HSM-backed KEKs.
- RBAC v2 gates who can: create keys, rotate keys, export audit, and request emergency key-rewraps.

Key custody models (short):
1) Redwood-managed KMS (default): Redwood KMS manages KEKs. Low friction, high telemetry.
2) Customer BYOK with HSM: customer supplies root key material or imports keys into a customer-controlled HSM. Redwood runs inside VPC and integrates via KMIP/CloudHSM. Strong isolation.
3) Hybrid: customer BYOK but keys wrapped by Redwood root (rare; requires contractual agreement).

RBAC v2 considerations (operational notes):
- Roles to provision in RBAC v2: key-admin, key-rotator, key-reader (for audits), key-emergency (for incident-only ops).
- Bind service accounts to 'key-rotator' with conditions: source IP range, MFA for human flows. Use time-limited tokens for rotation jobs.
- Emergency rotations must require 2 human approvers (two-person integrity) and are logged with escalation tags.
- Example policy fragments (pseudo):
  - allow: users with role == key-rotator to call kms:RotateKey on resource key/* when request.time within business-hours OR request.tag == emergency

Audit log schema (canonical fields we emit):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 string (UTC)
- event_id: UUIDv4
- principal_type: user | service_account | system
- principal_id: human-email or service-account-id
- action: create_key | rotate_key | import_key | schedule_rotation | decrypt_dek | rewrap_key | export_key_material | delete_key
- key_id: canonical KEK id (arn-like)
- key_version: integer or semantic version
- object_scope: bucket:<name> | db:<table> | global (if KEK used across scopes)
- result: success | failure
- error_code: short string (optional)
- source_ip: IP or cidr
- request_id: cloud provider request id or internal request id
- request_payload_hash: sha256 of sanitized payload (we avoid logging secrets)
- approvers: list (if rotation required approvals)
- notes: freeform (used for incident context)

Implementation notes for audit logs:
- All key-management events are writethrough to our immutable audit store and forwarded to SIEM. Logs must be ETL-ed so sensitive fields are redacted before leaving VPC.
- Retention: per compliance, KEK lifecycle logs retained 7 years (default for enterprise customers).

SIEM export mapping (examples for Splunk/Datadog/ELK):
- Splunk index: sec_kms
- Source type: redwood:kms:event
- Field mapping: timestamp -> _time, event_id -> event_id, principal_id -> user, action -> action, key_id -> key_id, object_scope->object_scope, result->status
- Recommended tags for SIEM alerts: high-risk (import_key OR export_key_material), emergency-rotation, repeated-failures

Evidence automation (goal):
- On any rotation or import/export event, generate an evidence bundle: {audit-log-entry, rotation-proposal, approver-IDs, automation-runbook-output (CLI stdout), pre/post validation hash} and store in evidence-bucket/<customer-id>/<key-id>/<timestamp>/bundle.json.gpg (encrypted with compliance key).
- Automation flow: rotation job submits to orchestration queue -> obtains time-limited key-rotator token from RBAC -> performs pre-checks -> executes rotation -> runs validation probes -> pushes bundle to evidence-bucket and updates ticket in Jira (SEC-XXX).

Key rotation procedure (operational run):
Pre-rotation checklist (must pass before starting):
- Verify current key_id, key_version, and that all dependent DEKs are recorded.
- Ensure snapshots/backups of metadata exist and are immutable for the rotation window. Path: s3://redwood-immutable-bak/<env>/<timestamp>/metadata.json
- Check SIEM connectivity and ensure audit-forwarding is healthy (alerting window <5m).
- Confirm RBAC token for rotation job is valid and bound to expected service account.
- Notify stakeholders via #sec-ops channel and create rotation ticket with target window.

Rotation steps (synthesized, non-vendor-specific):
1) Acquire lock: put-lock in datastore to prevent concurrent rotations on same KEK. CLI: redwood-kms lock acquire --key <key_id> --owner rotation-job-<id>.
2) Snapshot metadata and DEK index. CLI: redwood-kms metadata export --key <key_id> --out /tmp/meta.json
3) Generate new KEK version in HSM or KMS:
  - Hosted KMS: redwood-kms create-key-version --parent <key_id> --alg AES-256-GCM --usage encrypt/decrypt
  - HSM/BYOK import: follow vendor import flow (KMIP import or import-wrapped). Record import-transaction-id.
4) Rewrap DEKs: iterate over DEK index and call rewrap API: rewrap-dek --dek-id <id> --from-key <old_key_version> --to-key <new_key_version>. Rewrap jobs should run in parallel but limited concurrency (default 100 workers) and report per-object success.
5) Validation: select sampling checks (100 random objects + boundary buckets) and attempt decrypt using new KEK path. Record results to evidence bundle.
6) Promote new KEK version to ACTIVE (flip alias). This is the atomic switch. Ensure alias update is a single API call that is logged.
7) Post-checks: monitor application error rates, decryption failures, latency changes for 60m.
8) Rotate key metadata: increment key_version and write metadata record.
9) Release lock and close ticket with evidence bundle.

Rollback plan (if problems observed):
- If rewrap failures exceed threshold (default 1% errors or any customer-visible failures), revert alias to old key version (atomic alias switch) and stop rewrap workers. Keep rewrap queue paused and open incident.
- If alias flip is already done and decryption issues arise, new plan: rewrap with fallback worker that uses old key to re-encrypt DEKs then roll new key slowly. This is complex — escalate to Sec Eng and SRE.

Emergency rotation (short timeline):
- Two-person approval required (approver IDs must be present in audit entry).
- Use emergency rotation token with reduced TTL (15m).
- Notify customers per contract if KEK compromise suspected (follow incident disclosure playbook).

Testing & validation matrix (ops tests to run post-rotation):
- Functional: decrypt sample objects (per region, per storage-backend)
- Performance: 95th latency for decrypt path unchanged (+/- 10%)
- Consistency: object hashes pre/post (if re-wrapped payload unchanged)
- Audit: entries for each step exist and are forwarded to SIEM (verify with query: action=rotate_key AND key_id=<id>)

Operational automation snippets (examples):
- Rewrap loop (pseudo CLI):
  for dek in $(redwood-kms dek list --key old-key-v1); do
    rewrap-dek --dek-id $dek --to-key new-key-v2 || echo \"REWRAP_FAIL $dek\" >> /tmp/rewrap-failures
  done
- Healthcheck (post-rotation):
  curl -sS https://internal-health/redwood-kms/health | jq .reewrap_status

SIEM alert examples (playbook):
- High priority: event where action==export_key_material OR action==import_key with principal_type==user and not in allowlist -> create P1 ticket, notify SOC.
- Medium: repeated rotate_key failures > 5 within 10m -> auto-open rotation-ops ticket and page on-call.

Evidence retention and packaging details:
- Evidence bundle fields: {manifest.json, audit.log (filtered), pre-meta.json, post-meta.json, rewrap-summary.csv, validation-output.txt}
- Each bundle GPG-encrypted with compliance key and stored in immutable bucket with object lock + versioning.

Operational checklist (quick):
- [ ] Create rotation ticket and schedule window
- [ ] Preflight checks pass (backups, SIEM, RBAC token)
- [ ] Acquire lock
- [ ] Create new KEK version
- [ ] Run rewrap workers (monitor failures)
- [ ] Validate samples
- [ ] Flip alias to active
- [ ] Post-monitor 60m
- [ ] Publish evidence bundle and close ticket

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Decide default concurrency per tenant for rewrap jobs (current heuristic: min(100, tenant_objects/1000)). Need perf-run to tune. @Priya to run benchmark.
- Append RBAC v2 condition examples into centralized policy library (link to Confluence).
- Add vendor-specific CLI sequences for Thales and AWS CloudHSM to this runbook (owner: Diego).
- Determine legal notice template for notifying customers in case of KEK compromise (legal & compliance).

Appendix: quick commands and sample SIEM query
- Query SIEM (Splunk) for rotation events for key X: index=sec_kms action=rotate_key key_id=\"arn:krw:key:prod:keyX\" | stats count by result,principal_id
- Locking CLI: redwood-kms lock acquire --key arn:krw:key:prod:keyX --owner rotation-2024-10-03-01
- Create key version (hosted): redwood-kms create-key-version --key arn:krw:key:prod:keyX --algo AES-256-GCM

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc lightweight and operational (the deep design lives in KMS-Architecture confluence).
- When running a dry-run, use --no-alias-flip to practice rewraps. Add dry-run checklist to automation toolset.

Contact / escalation:
- Primary on-call: sec-ops-oncall rotation per PagerDuty
- Escalation: Sec Eng (Diego Morales) -> Head of Security (Avery Chen)

End of runbook.
